subject.title: [Feature]: Browser sandbox should support non-Docker backends (external CDP/noVNC endpoint)

question: Should OpenClaw add a narrow external CDP/noVNC endpoint config for sandbox browsers now, or design a backend-owned sandbox-browser contract before exposing this public surface?
rationale: The request changes public sandbox config and browser-control security boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the endpoint shape, lifecycle ownership, or security requirements.

options.title: Design backend-owned contract
options.body: Add a versioned sandbox-browser backend or external-endpoint contract with explicit CDP auth, noVNC, SSRF, lifecycle, docs, and tests before landing user-facing config.

options.title: Land narrow endpoint config
options.body: Add external endpoint fields only if maintainers accept a smaller public config surface and specify strict validation, redaction, reachability, and security behavior up front.

options.title: Defer to broader browser backend work
options.body: Keep this issue open but require the broader browser backend/plugin design to own sandbox-browser endpoints rather than adding a separate one-off path.

recommendation.title: Design backend-owned contract
recommendation.body: Add a versioned sandbox-browser backend or external-endpoint contract with explicit CDP auth, noVNC, SSRF, lifecycle, docs, and tests before landing user-facing config.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across sandbox browser policy, backend docs, and OpenShell sandbox seams relevant to this product/security choice.
